headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 13 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: A day for the attackers? Today’s course between Almuñécar and Loja (192.8 km) is packed with uphills (3,404 metres of elevation gain), including the cat. 1 climb of the Alto de la Venta de la Cebada. This demanding ascent features early in the stage, before the Alto del Legionario, and then the Puerto de Granada to enter the final 50 kilometres of the stage. Then, it’s essentially the downhill and a flat run-in to the finish. The neutral start is set at 12:20, the start proper at 12:41 after an 8 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Welcome to Granada
subtext: Today's stage is entirely set in the province of Granada, a staple of La Vuelta and particularly of the 2026 edition. Granada was a stage town already in the first La Vuelta (1935). It has hosted the Gran Salida in 2005 and 2008. Next week-end, it will host the finale for the first time in the history of the Spanish Grand Tour. The last stage winner in the province of Granada is Adam Yates, in 2024 (stage 9, Motril > Granada).

headline: On Carlos Rodriguez’s roads
subtext: Almuñécar make its debut as La Vuelta stage town*. It is the hometown of Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos), who was born here on 2 February 2001. The Spanish climber is taking part in La Vuelta for the third time. In 2022, he wore Spain’s national champion and finished 6th overall. In 2024, he was 10th. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Happy birthday Marc
subtext: Marc Brustenga (Kern Pharma) turns 27 today on the roads of his first Grand Tour.

headline: Rodriguez: "As a child who loved cycling, I always enjoyed going to watch the professionals, my idols"
subtext: Carlos Rodríguez (Netcompany Ineos) starts from his hometown today: “I hadn’t asked for it, but it’s much appreciated. It’s always special to set off from where you were born, from where you’re from. So, anyway, let’s enjoy today, because it doesn’t happen every day. Yes, there’s always been a stage that passed nearby or went through the village; as a child who loved cycling, I always enjoyed going to watch the professionals, my idols. Nowadays, being part of this peloton is something very special, and even more so with the start here. I hope to get back to my best form, to perform well. And, above all, to enjoy this experience, to enjoy La Vuelta as much as I can. And I hope that my enjoyment will rub off on them too, and that they’ll have a good time, whether watching on TV or cheering from the roadside.”

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with an 8 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) did more than resist the assault led by Felix Gall and Decathlon CMA CGM at CalarAlto - the Spanish climber powered away from his rivals to extend his lead in the overall standings. Primoz Roglic (RedBull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is still second, with a gap of 1’45’’, while Gall now trails by 2’06’’. At 3’53’’, Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) passed Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), who resisted Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious). The British youngster trails by 4’29’’, and his Slovenian rival by 4’59’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Another breakaway, another intermediate sprint won, and Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) pushed distally to 194 points. His teammate Matthew Brennan is still second, with 117 points, and Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) follows with 96 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) made the most of yesterday’s many summits to pull away at the top of the mountains standings: 52 points for the Colombian climber, while Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) has 30 after he led the way on the first summits of the day. Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) made a significant jump in the best young riders standings with his victory at Calar Alto - the Slovenian youngster is back within 30 seconds of the white jersey, but Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) held on to the lead after a rough day. Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) is now in thethird place (+11’39’’).

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Felix Gall, Gregor Mühlberger and Léo Bisiaux at the front, Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance yesterday and extended their lead in the overall team standings. Bahrain Victorious are now second (+1h06’11’’) ahead of Netcompany Ineos (+1h06’31’’).

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will race with a distinctive bib again as he was named the most combative rider for the second time (stages 7 and 12).

headline: Stage 13 is ON!
subtext: The many contenders for the breakaway can battle it out!

subtext: Four riders currently lead the way but the battle rages on.

headline: 22 seconds
subtext: Dolen Novak (UAE Emirates), Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Fabio Van Den Bossche (Soudal Quick-Step) and Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla) are the first attackers to make a difference.

headline: Flying past Salobreña
subtext: Next to Almuñécar, Salobreña (km 5 on today’s route) hosted the start of stage 12 of La Vuelta 22. Richard Carapaz won at Peñas Blanca, where Remco Evenepoel retained La Roja ahead of Primoz Roglic and Enric Mas. Marco Brenner (5th), José Manuel Diaz (12th), Alexey Lutsenko (26th), Carlos Canal (28th) and Ivo Oliveira (77th) were part of the breakaway with Carapaz.

headline: The gap slightly increases: 40'' at km 12

headline: Kern Pharma want to make the break
subtext: A rider from the Spanish team has accelerated again after Urko Berrade was reeled in. He was second yesterday, a result that "certainly comes at a good time, halfway through the Vuelta, in the third breakaway I’ve been part of", he said at the start." I learnt from the mistakes of previous breakaways; it went really well for me all day. I was beaten by a very strong rider – all I can do is congratulate him, recover from yesterday and keep trying."

headline: Into the final 100 kilometres
subtext: The eleven leaders keep pushing. Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos) just went down in a turn. He rapidly got back up. The chasers trail by a minute. The gap to the peloton has increased to four minutes.

headline: De la Cruz has crashed in the chase group
subtext: The Spaniard suffers from his right shoulder but he gets back up and resumes racing. Axel Laurance is also back in action after his crash.

headline: De la Cruz is caught by the bunch
subtext: Movistar and EF Education-EasyPost work together to control the gap. They are 4 minutes behind the leaders, and two and a half minutes behind the Skjelmose group.

headline: Crash for David de la Cruz
Van Aert: "I would love to prioritise the stage win today"
subtext: At the start, Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) was hoping to be the key player in today's stage: "It would mean I have good legs, and then I can be out there. It’s complicated terrain, it’s still a lot of climbing. For sure, the second part of the stage should suit me, so I hope to be there today. I would love to prioritise the stage win today."

headline: Albanese was also wary of Brennan
subtext: Vincenzo Albanese (EF Education-EasyPost) made the breakaway with a strong effort to close the gap to the lead group. "I think today is 50-50, maybe for the breakaway or maybe sprint finish”, the Italian fast man said at the start. “It depends of Visma, Cofidis and FDJ." These three teams have put several riders at the front after an intense battle. Does it depend of Wout van Aert? "I think also Brennan”, Albanese said.

headline: 80 kilometres to go
subtext: The ten leaders are 1'20'' ahead of the peloton, while the peloton control the gap at 4 minutes. The riders are on a flat section leading to the intermediate sprint (Tocon, km 145) and then the final climb of the day, Puerto de Granada (cat. 2, summit at km 155.4).

headline: Kron: "I had some hard years but I'm really on the way back"
subtext: Among the ten leaders, Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) is looking for his first pro victory since Barcelona in La Vuelta 23: "I hope it will be in La Vuelta also. [Today] I will try, we already tried some days but I think today is a good day. I had some hard years but I'm really on the way back. I feel good and I hope to get a win, but at least we’re trying every day. I think [today] there will be a big fight [for the breakaway] like the other days, and then I hope to go in the climb with a good group."

headline: The chasers get closer: 1 minute
subtext: Meanwhile, the gap to the bunch extends to 4'15''. That means Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) is gaining 3'15'' and moving into the overall top 5.

headline: The average speed after 3 hours: 40.8 km/h
subtext: The pace has been really demanding with the heat and the many hills.

headline: Gearing to make history in Loja
subtext: Loja is a La Vuelta stage town for the second time after hosting the start on day 6 of the 1990 edition - so it will be the first finish here. The race headed to Ubrique, where Jesper Worre tooth win and Julian Gorospe claimed the overall lead. Also part of the day’s breakaway, Italy’s Marco Giovannetti gained four minutes on the peloton and eventually won La Vuelta a couple of weeks later in Madrid, ahead of Pedro Delgado (+1’28’’).

headline: 60 kilometres to go
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike), Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), Clément Berthet, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Andreas Kron, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Vincenzo Albanese (EF Education-EasyPost), Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana), and Lars Craps (Lotto Intermarché) have increased their lead: +1'30'' Chase group +4'40'' Peloton

headline: Martin-Guyonnet helps Berthet move up in the overall standings
subtext: Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United) is known for his ability to gain time and places in the overall standings through long range attacks. Today, he's setting the pace at the front for Clément Berthet, who started the day 11th and is already set to enter the GC top 10 after Gregor Mühlberger (Decathlon CMA CGM) crashed out of the race. "I hope I’ll have opportunities to pick up some time via a breakaway", Berthet said yesterday at the start. "It’s not impossible that it could happen today. Nor can I afford to give it my all trying to join a breakaway that might not make it to the finish. It’s a balance I need to strike. I think there are certain days that lend themselves to this more than others. You’d have to ask Guillaume - he’s the expert on the subject. But yes, there’s certainly a bit of strategy involved in it all."

headline: The final climb of the day
subtext: The road rises up the Puerto de Granada: 7.4 km at 5.6%. The chasers are hald a minute behind the leaders. The peloton just passed the intermediate sprint: 4'45''. With agap of 4'15'' between the chase and the peloton, Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek) is fourth in the virtual GC.

headline: Wout van Aert wins stage 13 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: His first victory in this edition after he claimed three in 2024!
